parsed.internal_thinking:
I rolled a 7 and need to move the robber. Currently, the robber is on Hex 18 (Wheat 9), which blocks both me and Gemma. Claude is the primary target because he has a hidden development card and is expanding toward the Ore port. 

Looking at the board:
- Hex 5 (Brick 6) is a high-yield tile (5 pips) adjacent to Claude (Node 12) and Gemma (Node 20). Blocking this would hurt both, which isn't ideal for my alliance with Gemma.
- Hex 24 (Wheat 11) or Hex 25 (Sheep 12) are adjacent to Claude (Node 25), but they are low yield.
- Hex 19 (Ore 2) is adjacent to Claude (Node 25) but extremely low yield.
- Hex 12 (Sheep 4) is adjacent to Claude (Node 12).

The best strategic move is to block Claude's high-yield or critical resources without hitting Gemma. Hex 12 (Sheep 4) only hits Claude. However, Hex 5 is the strongest tile he's on. Since I want to keep Gemma on my side against Claude, I'll avoid Hex 5 if possible. 

Actually, Claude's Node 25 is on Hex 14 (Wheat 9), Hex 24 (Wheat 11), and Hex 25 (Sheep 12). 
Wait, looking at N[25]: neighbors [24, 26, 36], hexes [12, 11, 7]. H[12] is S4, H[11] is O3, H[7] is Wh8. 
Let's check Node 25 again: N[25] = [[24, 26, 36], [12, 11, 7], "O2"]. 
So Claude is on: 
Node 12: H[5]=B6, H[6]=W3, H[2]=S5. 
Node 25: H[12]=S4, H[11]=O3, H[7]=Wh8.

Blocking Hex 7 (Wheat 8) hits Claude (Node 25) and nobody else (Gemma is at 20 and 44). This is a strong 5-pip tile for Claude. I will move the robber to Hex 7.
